/books/consider-phlebas/read/title-epigr.en:
Gentile or Jew
O you who turn the wheel and look to windward,
Consider Phlebas, who was once handsome and tall as you.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/title-epigr.zh:
无论你是外邦人，还是犹太人，
啊，你这转动舵轮、迎风眺望的人，
请念及Phlebas——他也曾像你一样，俊美而高大。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: 1. Sorpen
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: 1. Sorpen

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: The level was at his top lip now. Even with his head pressed hard back against the stones of the cell wall his nose was only just above the surface. He wasn't going to get his hands free in time; he was going to drown.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: 水面已经涨到他的上唇。即使把后脑勺死死抵在牢房的石壁上，鼻子也才勉强露出水面。他来不及挣脱双手了；他要被淹死了。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: In the darkness of the cell, in its stink and warmth, while the sweat ran over his brows and tightly closed eyes and his trance went on and on, one part of his mind tried to accustom him to the idea of his own death. But, like an unseen insect buzzing in a quiet room, there was something else, something that would not go away, was of no use, and only annoyed. It was a sentence, irrelevant and pointless and so old he'd forgotten where he had heard or read it, and it went round and round the inside of his head like a marble spun round the inside of a jug:
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: 牢房里漆黑、恶臭、闷热。汗水流过眉头和紧闭的双眼，他一直沉浸在恍惚状态中，意识的一部分试着让他接受自己即将死去的事实。然而，还有一样东西，像安静房间里一只看不见的飞虫，嗡嗡作响，挥之不去，毫无用处，只让人烦躁。那是一句话，既不相干，也毫无意义，而且太过久远，他早已忘记是在哪里听见或读到的。它在他脑子里转了一圈又一圈，像在罐子里打转的一颗弹珠：

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: The Jinmoti of Bozlen Two kill the hereditary ritual assassins of the new Yearking's immediate family by drowning them in the tears of the Continental Empathaur in its Sadness Season.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: Bozlen Two的Jinmoti，会把新任年王直系亲属的世袭仪式刺客淹死在大陆共情兽悲伤季的泪水中。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: At one point, shortly after his ordeal had begun and he was only part-way into his trance, he had wondered what would happen if he threw up. It had been when the palace kitchens—about fifteen or sixteen floors above, if his calculations were correct—had sent their waste down the sinuous network of plumbing that led to the sewercell. The gurgling, watery mess had dislodged some rotten food from the last time some poor wretch had drowned in filth and garbage, and that was when he felt he might vomit. It had been almost comforting to work out that it would make no difference to the time of his death.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: 受刑刚开始不久，他还没有完全进入恍惚状态时，曾想过：要是自己吐了，会怎么样？当时，宫殿厨房——如果他算得没错，大约在上面十五六层——正把废物倒进那套蜿蜒曲折、通往这间污水牢的管道里。咕噜作响的稀烂污物冲起了一些腐败的食物残渣，那是上一个可怜虫淹死在污秽和垃圾里时留下的。他就是在那一刻觉得自己可能会吐。他想明白，吐不吐都不会改变自己的死期，竟然多少感到了一点安慰。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: Then he had wondered—in that state of nervous frivolity which sometimes afflicts those who can do nothing but wait in a situation of mortal threat—whether crying would speed his death. In theory it would, though in practical terms it was irrelevant; but that was when the sentence started to roll round in his head.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: 接着，他又想：哭会不会让自己死得更快？面对致命威胁却只能坐等时，人有时会陷入一种既紧张又轻浮的状态，他当时正是如此。理论上会，实际上却无关紧要。也就是这时，那句话开始在他脑子里打转。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: The Jinmoti of Bozlen Two kill the hereditary ritual...
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: Bozlen Two的Jinmoti，会把世袭仪式……

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: The liquid, which he could hear and feel and smell all too clearly—and could probably have seen with his far from ordinary eyes had they been open—washed briefly up to touch the bottom of his nose. He felt it block his nostrils, filling them with a stench that made his stomach heave. But he shook his head, tried to force his skull even further back against the stones, and the foul broth fell away. He blew down and could breathe again.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: 那液体的声音、触感和气味，他都感受得再清楚不过——如果睁开眼睛，凭他那双远非寻常的眼睛，大概也能看见。液体一度涌上来，碰到了他的鼻底。他感觉鼻孔被堵住，恶臭灌进来，熏得胃里一阵翻腾。但他摇了摇头，设法把后脑勺更用力地往石壁上挤，那锅污汤便又退了下去。他朝下呼了一口气，又能呼吸了。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: There wasn't long now. He checked his wrists again, but it was no good. It would take another hour or more, and he had only minutes, if he was lucky.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: 时间不多了。他又检查了一遍手腕，还是不行。还得一个小时，甚至更久；而他就算走运，也只剩下几分钟。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: The trance was breaking anyway. He was returning to almost total consciousness, as though his brain wanted fully to appreciate his own death, its own extinction. He tried to think of something profound, or to see his life flash in front of him, or suddenly to remember some old love, a long-forgotten prophecy or premonition, but there was nothing, just an empty sentence, and the sensations of drowning in other people's dirt and waste.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: 反正，恍惚状态也在消退。他的意识几乎完全恢复了，仿佛大脑非要充分领略自己的死亡、自己的消灭不可。他试着想些深刻的东西，或让一生在眼前闪过，或突然忆起一段旧日恋情、一则早已遗忘的预言或预感，可是什么也没有。只有一句空洞的话，以及淹死在别人污秽和排泄物里的感觉。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: You old bastards, he thought. One of their few strokes of humour or originality had been devising an elegant, ironic way of death. How fitting it must feel to them, dragging their decrepit frames to the banquet-hall privies, literally to defecate all over their enemies, and thereby kill them.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: 你们这些老王八蛋，他想。他们那点少得可怜的幽默和创意，有一项就是设计出了这种精巧而讽刺的死法。他们拖着衰朽的身子，走进宴会厅的厕所，真真切切地把屎拉在敌人头上，用这种方式杀死敌人——想必觉得再合适不过。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: The air pressure built up, and a distant, groaning rumble of liquid signalled another flushing from above. You old bastards. Well, I hope at least you kept your promise, Balveda.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: 气压渐渐升高，远处传来低沉的、仿佛呻吟般的水声，说明上面又在冲水了。你们这些老王八蛋。好吧，Balveda，但愿你至少遵守了承诺。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: The Jinmoti of Bozlen Two kill the hereditary ritual... thought one part of his brain, as the pipes in the ceiling spluttered and the waste splashed into the warm mass of liquid which almost filled the cell. The wave passed over his face, then fell back to leave his nose free for a second and give him time to gulp a lungful of air. Then the liquid rose gently to touch the bottom of his nose again, and stayed there.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: Bozlen Two的Jinmoti，会把世袭仪式……他的部分意识这样想着。头顶的管道噗噗作响，污物溅进那团几乎填满牢房的温热液体里。浪头漫过他的脸，随后又退下去，让鼻子短暂露出了一秒钟，给了他猛吸一口气的时间。接着，液体又缓缓升到鼻底，停在那里。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: He held his breath.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: 他屏住了呼吸。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: It had hurt at first, when they had hung him up. His hands, tied inside tight leather pouches, were directly above his head, manacled inside thick loops of iron bolted to the cell walls, which took all his weight. His feet were tied together and left to dangle inside an iron tube, also attached to the wall, which stopped him from taking any weight on his feet and knees and at the same time prevented him from moving his legs more than a hand's breadth out from the wall or to either side. The tube ended just above his knees; above it there was only a thin and dirty loincloth to hide his ancient and grubby nakedness.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: 刚被吊起来时，是很疼的。他的双手各自紧紧裹在皮袋里，举在头顶，铐在牢房墙上用螺栓固定的粗铁环中，承受着全身的重量。双脚捆在一起，悬在一根同样固定于墙上的铁管里。铁管使他无法用脚或膝盖分担体重，也使双腿不论向前还是向两侧，都不能离开墙面超过一掌宽。管口刚过膝盖；再往上，只有一块又薄又脏的裆布，遮着他那衰老、污秽的裸体。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: He had shut off the pain from his wrists and shoulders even while the four burly guards, two of them perched on ladders, had secured him in place. Even so he could feel that niggling sensation at the back of his skull which told him that he ought to be hurting. That had lessened gradually as the level of waste in the small sewercell had risen and buoyed up his body.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: 四个壮实的卫兵把他固定在那里时——其中两个还站在梯子上——他就已经切断了手腕和肩膀传来的疼痛。即便如此，后脑深处仍有一种隐隐的感觉，提醒他：他本该疼痛。随着这间小小污水牢里的污物逐渐涨高，托起他的身体，那种感觉才慢慢减轻。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: He had started to go into a trance then, as soon as the guards left, though he knew it was probably hopeless. It hadn't lasted long; the cell door opened again within minutes, a metal walkway was lowered by a guard onto the damp flagstones of the cell floor, and light from the corridor washed into the darkness. He had stopped the Changing trance and craned his neck to see who his visitor might be.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: 卫兵一离开，他就开始进入恍惚状态，尽管他知道大概已经无望。但这状态没持续多久；几分钟后，牢门又开了。一名卫兵把一段金属踏桥放到牢房潮湿的石板地面上，走廊的灯光漫入黑暗。他中止了变形时的恍惚状态，伸长脖子，想看看来人是谁。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: Into the cell, holding a short staff glowing cool blue, stepped the stooped, grizzled figure of Amahain-Frolk, security minister for the Gerontocracy of Sorpen. The old man smiled at him and nodded approvingly, then turned to the corridor and, with a thin, discoloured hand, beckoned somebody standing outside the cell to step onto the short walkway and enter. He guessed it would be the Culture agent Balveda, and it was. She came lightly onto the metal boarding, looked round slowly, and fastened her gaze on him. He smiled and tried to nod in greeting, his ears rubbing on his naked arms.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: 走进牢房的是Amahain-Frolk，Sorpen元老政权的安全大臣。他身形佝偻，须发斑白，手里拿着一根泛着冷蓝色光芒的短杖。老人对他笑了笑，赞许地点点头，随后转向走廊，用那只枯瘦、肤色斑驳的手，招呼站在门外的人踏上短桥，进来。他猜是文明的特工Balveda，果然是她。她轻轻踏上金属桥板，缓缓环顾四周，最后把目光定在他身上。他笑了笑，试着点头致意，耳朵擦过自己裸露的双臂。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: 'Balveda! I thought I might see you again. Come to see the host of the party?' He forced a grin. Officially it was his banquet; he was the host. Another of the Gerontocracy's little jokes. He hoped his voice had shown no signs of fear.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: “Balveda！我就想，也许还能再见到你。来看看宴会的主人？”他挤出一脸笑容。名义上，这场宴会是他的，他是主人。这又是元老政权开的一个小玩笑。他希望自己的声音没有露出恐惧。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: Perosteck Balveda, agent of the Culture, a full head taller than the old man by her side and still strikingly handsome even in the pallid glow of the blue torch, shook her thin, finely made head slowly. Her short, black hair lay like a shadow on her skull.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: 文明特工Perosteck Balveda比身旁的老人高出整整一个头。即使在蓝色火炬惨淡的光照下，她仍然美得令人注目。她缓缓摇了摇那颗瘦削、轮廓精致的头。短短的黑发像一片阴影，贴在她的头上。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: 'No,' she said, 'I didn't want to see you, or say goodbye.'
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: “不，”她说，“我并不想来见你，也不想来道别。”

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: 'You put me here, Balveda,' he said quietly.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: “是你把我送到这里的，Balveda。”他轻声说。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: 'Yes, and there you belong,' Amahain-Frolk said, stepping as far forward on the platform as he could without overbalancing and having to step onto the damp floor. 'I wanted you tortured first, but Miss Balveda here'—the minister's high, scratchy voice echoed in the cell as he turned his head back to the woman?'pleaded for you, though God knows why. But that's where you belong all right; murderer.' He shook the staff at the almost naked man hanging on the dirty wall of the cell.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: “没错，你就该待在这里。”Amahain-Frolk在踏桥上尽可能地往前挪，既不失去平衡，也不必踏上潮湿的地面。“我本来想先让你受刑，不过，这位Balveda小姐”——大臣转头看向那个女人，尖细沙哑的嗓音在牢房里回荡——“替你求了情，天知道为什么。但你确实就该待在这里，杀人犯。”他朝那个几乎赤裸、吊在脏污石壁上的男人晃了晃短杖。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: Balveda looked at her feet, just visible under the hem of the long, plain grey gown she wore. A circular pendant on a chain around her neck glinted in the light from the corridor outside. Amahain-Frolk had stepped back beside her, holding the shining staff up and squinting at the captive.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: Balveda低头看着自己的脚，长长的素灰色裙摆下，只露出一点脚尖。颈间链子上的圆形吊坠，在外面走廊的灯光里闪了一下。Amahain-Frolk退回她身旁，举起发光的短杖，眯着眼睛打量囚犯。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: 'You know, even now I could almost swear that was Egratin hanging there. I can...' He shook his gaunt, bony head. '... I can hardly believe it isn't, not until he opens his mouth, anyway. My God, these Changers are dangerous frightening things!' He turned to Balveda. She smoothed her hair at the nape of her neck and looked down at the old man.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: “你知道吗？就算到了现在，我也差点要发誓，吊在那里的是Egratin。我真……”他摇了摇那颗瘦得只剩骨头的脑袋。“……真不敢相信那不是他，至少在他开口之前是这样。我的天，这些变形者实在是危险又可怕的东西！”他转向Balveda。她抚平颈后的头发，低头看着老人。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: 'They are also an ancient and proud people, Minister, and there are very few of them left. May I ask you one more time? Please? Let him live. He might be?'
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: “他们也是一个古老而自尊的种族，大臣。而且，他们已经所剩无几了。我能再请求您一次吗？求您了，留他一命。他也许还能——”

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: The Gerontocrat waved a thin and twisted hand at her, his face distorting in a grimace. 'No! You would do well, Miss Balveda, not to keep asking for this... this assassin, this murderous, treacherous... spy, to be spared. Do you think we take the cowardly murder and impersonation of one of our Outworld ministers lightly? What damage this... thing could have caused! Why, when we arrested it two of our guards died just from being scratched! Another is blind for life after this monster spat in his eye! However,' Amahain-Frolk sneered at the man chained to the wall, 'we took those teeth out. And his hands are tied so that he can't even scratch himself.' He turned to Balveda again. 'You say they are few? I say good; there will soon be one less.' The old man narrowed his eyes as he looked at the woman. 'We are grateful to you and your people for exposing this fraud and murderer, but do not think that gives you the right to tell us what to do. There are some in the Gerontocracy who want nothing to do with any outside influence, and their voices grow in volume by the day as the war comes closer. You would do well not to antagonise those of us who do support your cause.'
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: 那位元老朝她挥了挥枯瘦、扭曲的手，面孔皱成一团。“不行！Balveda小姐，你最好别再为这个……这个刺客，这个凶残、奸诈的……间谍求饶了。你以为我们会轻轻放过这种卑鄙的罪行——杀害我们的一位外星事务大臣，再冒充他？这个……东西本来能造成多大的破坏！我们逮捕它时，两名卫兵只是被它抓伤，就死了！还有一个被这怪物往眼睛里啐了一口，从此瞎了一辈子！不过，”Amahain-Frolk朝那个被铐在墙上的男人冷笑，“我们已经把那些牙齿拔掉了。它的手也捆起来了，连自己都抓不了。”他又转向Balveda。“你说他们所剩无几？我说好，很快就又要少一个了。”老人眯起眼睛，望着她。“我们感谢你和你的同胞，揭穿了这个骗子、这个杀人犯，但别以为这样就能对我们发号施令。元老政权里有些人，不愿受到任何外界影响。随着战火逼近，他们的声音一天比一天响。对我们这些确实支持你们的人，你最好别把我们也惹恼了。”

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: Balveda pursed her lips and looked down at her feet again, clasping her slender hands behind her back. Amahain-Frolk had turned back to the man hanging on the wall, wagging the staff in his direction as he spoke. 'You will soon be dead, impostor, and with you die your masters' plans for the domination of our peaceful system! The same fate awaits them if they try to invade us. We and the Culture are?'
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: Balveda抿着嘴唇，又低头望向自己的脚，纤细的双手扣在背后。Amahain-Frolk转回身，边说边朝墙上的男人晃着短杖。“冒牌货，你很快就要死了！你死了，你主子妄图统治我们这片和平星系的计划，也就跟着完了！他们要是敢入侵，下场也一样。我们和文明是——”

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: He shook his head as best he could and roared back, 'Frolk, you're an idiot!' The old man shrank away as though hit. The Changer went on, 'Can't you see you're going to be taken over anyway? Probably by the Idirans, but if not by them then by the Culture. You don't control your own destinies any more; the war's stopped all that. Soon this whole sector will be part of the front, unless you make it part of the Idiran sphere. I was only sent in to tell you what you should have known anyway—not to cheat you into something you'd regret later. For God's sake, man, the Idirans won't eat you?'
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: 他竭力摇着头，吼了回去：“Frolk，你是个白痴！”老人像挨了一下似的往后一缩。变形者继续说道：“你还看不出来吗？你们无论如何都会被接管。多半是Idirans；不是他们，就会是文明。你们已经不能掌握自己的命运了，战争把这一切都结束了。用不了多久，这整片星区都会变成前线，除非你们主动把它划进Idiran的势力范围。我被派来，不过是告诉你们本来就该明白的事——不是哄你们去做什么以后会后悔的决定。看在上帝的分上，老兄，Idirans又不会吃了你——”

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: 'Ha! They look as though they could! Monsters with three feet; invaders, killers, infidels... You want us to link with them? With three-strides tall-monsters? To be ground under their hooves? To have to worship their false gods?'
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: “哈！他们看起来可真像会吃人！三只脚的怪物；入侵者、杀人犯、异教徒……你要我们和他们结盟？和那些三大步高的怪物？让他们用蹄子把我们踩成肉泥？还得去拜他们的假神？”

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: 'At least they have a God, Frolk. The Culture doesn't.' The ache in his arms was coming back as he concentrated on talking. He shifted as best he could and looked down at the minister. 'They at least think the same way you do. The Culture doesn't.'
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: “至少他们有上帝，Frolk。文明没有。”他一心说话，双臂的酸痛又回来了。他尽力挪动身子，低头望着大臣。“至少他们的想法和你们一样。文明不一样。”

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: 'Oh no, my friend, oh no.' Amahain-Frolk held one hand up flat to him and shook his head. 'You won't sow seeds of discord like that.'
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: “不，我的朋友，不。”Amahain-Frolk朝他摊开一只手，摇了摇头。“你用这种话，是挑拨不了我们的。”

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: 'My God, you stupid old man,' he laughed. 'You want to know who the real representative of the Culture is on this planet? It's not her,' he nodded at the woman, 'it's that powered flesh-slicer she has following her everywhere, her knife missile. She might make the decisions, it might do what she tells it, but it's the real emissary. That's what the Culture's about: machines. You think because Balveda's got two legs and soft skin you should be on her side, but it's the Idirans who are on the side of life in this war?'
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: “我的天，你这蠢老头。”他笑了。“你想知道，这颗星球上真正代表文明的是谁吗？不是她，”他朝那个女人点了点头，“是那台一直跟在她身边的切肉机器——她的刀式导弹。也许由她作决定，也许它听她的命令，但真正的使者是它。文明的本质就是这个：机器。你以为Balveda长着两条腿，皮肤柔软，就该站在她那边。可在这场战争里，站在生命这一边的是Idirans——”

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: 'Well, you will shortly be on the other side of that.' The Gerontocrat snorted and glanced at Balveda, who was looking from under lowered brows at the man chained to the wall. 'Let us go, Miss Balveda,' Amahain-Frolk said as he turned and took the woman's arm to guide her from the cell. 'This... thing's presence smells more than the cell.'
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: “好吧，你很快就要站到生命的另一边去了。”那位元老哼了一声，瞥向Balveda。她眉头低垂，望着被铐在墙上的男人。“我们走吧，Balveda小姐。”Amahain-Frolk转过身，拉住女人的胳膊，要把她带出牢房。“这个……东西，比牢房本身还臭。”

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: Balveda looked up at him then, ignoring the dwarfed minister as he tried to pull her to the door. She gazed right at the prisoner with her clear, black-irised eyes and held her hands out from her sides. 'I'm sorry,' she said to him.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: Balveda这才抬起头，不理会身旁那个矮小的老大臣如何把她往门口拉。她用清澈的、虹膜漆黑的眼睛直视囚犯，双手从身体两侧微微摊开。“对不起。”她对他说。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: 'Believe it or not, that's rather how I feel,' he replied, nodding. 'Just promise me you'll eat and drink very little tonight, Balveda. I'd like to think there was one person up there on my side, and it might as well be my worst enemy.' He had meant it to be defiant and funny, but it sounded only bitter; he looked away from the woman's face.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: “信不信由你，我倒也有点这种感觉。”他点头答道。“只要答应我，今晚少吃、少喝一点，Balveda。我想，至少上面还能有一个人站在我这边；那个人是我的头号敌人，也没什么不好。”他本想说得既挑衅又诙谐，出口却只有苦涩。他把目光从女人脸上移开。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: 'I promise,' Balveda said. She let herself be led to the door, and the blue light waned in the dank cell. She stopped right at the door. By sticking his head painfully far out he could just see her. The knife missile was there, too, he noticed, just inside the room; probably there all the time, but he hadn't noticed its sleek, sharp little body hovering there in the darkness. He looked into Balveda's dark eyes as the knife missile moved.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: “我答应。”Balveda说。她任由老人把自己领到门口，潮湿牢房里的蓝光渐渐暗了下去。就在门边，她停住了。他把头伸得很远，疼得厉害，才勉强能看见她。他注意到，刀式导弹也在，就在门内；它大概一直都在那里，只是他没注意到那具流线型、锋利的小小机体悬浮在黑暗中。刀式导弹动了，他望进Balveda那双深色的眼睛。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: For a second he thought Balveda had instructed the tiny machine to kill him now—quietly and quickly while she blocked Amahain-Frolk's view—and his heart thudded. But the small device simply floated past Balveda's face and out into the corridor. Balveda raised one hand in a gesture of farewell.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: 有那么一秒，他以为Balveda命令那小机器现在就杀了他——趁她挡住Amahain-Frolk的视线，悄悄地、迅速地动手——心脏顿时猛跳。但那个小装置只是掠过Balveda的脸，飘进了走廊。Balveda抬起一只手，作了个告别的姿势。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: 'Bora Horza Gobuchul,' she said, 'goodbye.' She turned quickly, stepped from the platform and out of the cell. The walkway was hoisted out and the door slammed, scraping rubber flanges over the grimy floor and hissing once as the internal seals made it watertight. He hung there, looking down at an invisible floor for a moment before going back into the trance that would Change his wrists, thin them down so that he could escape. But something about the solemn, final way Balveda had spoken his name had crushed him inside, and he knew then, if not before, that there was no escape.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: “Bora Horza Gobuchul，”她说，“再见。”她猛地转过身，踏下金属桥，走出了牢房。踏桥被吊了起来，门砰地关上，橡胶密封边擦过污脏的地面。内部密封装置嘶地响了一声，把门封得滴水不漏。他吊在那里，低头望着看不见的地板，过了一会儿，又试着进入恍惚状态，改变手腕的形状，让它们变细，好挣脱出去。可Balveda念出他名字时，那种郑重而决绝的语气，已经把他心里的什么东西压碎了。直到这时——如果不是更早——他终于明白，自己逃不出去了。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: ... by drowning them in the tears...
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: ……淹死在泪水中……

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: His lungs were bursting! His mouth quivered, his throat was gagging, the filth was in his ears but he could hear a great roaring, see lights though it was black dark. His stomach muscles started to go in and out, and he had to clamp his jaw to stop his mouth opening for air that wasn't there. Now. No... now he had to give in. Not yet... surely now. Now, now, now, any second; surrender to this awful black vacuum inside him... he had to breathe... now!
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: 肺要炸开了！嘴唇颤抖，喉咙一阵阵抽紧。污物灌进耳朵，他却听见巨大的轰鸣；明明一片漆黑，却看见了亮光。腹部肌肉开始一收一缩，他不得不咬紧牙关，免得张嘴去吸根本不存在的空气。现在。不……现在，他必须放弃了。还不行……可现在总该到时候了。现在，现在，现在，就在下一秒；屈服于体内这个可怕、漆黑的真空……他必须呼吸……现在！

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: Before he had time to open his mouth he was smashed against the wall—punched against the stones as though some immense iron fist had slammed into him. He blew out the stale air from his lungs in one convulsive breath. His body was suddenly cold, and every part of it next to the wall throbbed with pain. Death, it seemed, was weight, pain, cold... and too much light...
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: 还没来得及张嘴，他就被猛地砸向墙壁——像有一只硕大的铁拳把他轰在石头上。肺里的浊气一下子全喷了出来。身体骤然冰冷，贴着墙的每一处都痛得突突直跳。死亡，看来就是重量、疼痛、寒冷……还有过于刺眼的光……

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: He brought his head up. He moaned at the light. He tried to see, tried to hear. What was happening? Why was he breathing? Why was he so damn heavy again? His body was tearing his arms from their sockets; his wrists were cut almost to the bone. Who had done this to him?
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: 他抬起头。强光让他呻吟起来。他试着看，试着听。发生了什么？为什么他还能呼吸？为什么他又变得这么该死地沉？身体正把两条胳膊从肩窝里往外扯；手腕被割得几乎见骨。是谁把他弄成了这样？

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: Where the wall had been facing him there was a very large and ragged hole which extended beneath the level of the cell floor. All the ordure and garbage had burst out of that. The last few trickles hissed against the hot sides of the breach, producing steam which curled around the figure standing blocking most of the brilliant light from outside, in the open air of Sorpen. The figure was three metres tall and looked vaguely like a small armoured spaceship sitting on a tripod of thick legs. Its helmet looked big enough to contain three human heads, side by side. Held almost casually in one gigantic hand was a plasma cannon which Horza would have needed both arms just to lift; the creature's other fist gripped a slightly larger gun. Behind it, nosing in towards the hole, came an Idiran gun-platform, lit vividly by the light of explosions which Horza could now feel through the iron and stones he was attached to. He raised his head to the giant standing in the breach and tried to smile.
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: 正对着他的那面墙不见了，取而代之的是一个又大又参差的洞，洞口一直延伸到牢房地面以下。所有粪污和垃圾都从那里冲了出去。最后几股污水淌过洞口滚烫的边缘，发出嘶嘶声，化成蒸汽，缠绕着一个挡住了大部分外界强光的身影。那身影站在Sorpen的露天里，高达三米，看起来有点像一艘架在三条粗腿上的小型装甲飞船。它的头盔大得足以并排装下三个人头。一只巨手像是不费什么力气就握着一门等离子炮，Horza恐怕得用两只胳膊才能把它举起来；另一只拳头里攥着一件略大些的武器。它身后，一座Idiran炮台正缓缓探向洞口。爆炸的火光把它照得分外鲜明，Horza甚至能透过束缚自己的铁具和石墙感到爆炸的震动。他抬起头，望着站在缺口中的巨人，试着笑了笑。

/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.en: 'Well,' he croaked, then spluttered and spat, 'you lot certainly took your time.'
/books/consider-phlebas/read/1-sorpen.zh: “好吧，”他嘶声说道，随后呛咳了几下，啐出一口污物，“你们可真是不紧不慢啊。”
